{"chunk_id":"R2-2111590-001","collection":"ran2_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":[],"tdocNumber":"R2-2111590","title":"LS to RAN4 on L3 filter configuration"},"point_id":"11086798994254803757"}
 Source: RAN2 To: RAN4 Cc: Contact Person: Name: Fangli XU E-mail Address: fangli_xu@apple.com 1. Overall Description RAN2 discussed the sample rate X(ms) associated to the L3 filter configuration (i.e. filterCoefficient k) in RAN2#116e meeting. And RAN2’s common understanding on the sample rate X is that the UE and gNB have the same understanding on it. RAN2 also think the sample rate X is only determined when the UE receives the L3 filter configuration, and will not be changed afterward, e.g. not changed due to SCell activation/deactivation, BWP switching, etc. Since the sample rate X is not defined in RRC spec, but just refers to TS38.133, RAN2 would like to check with RAN4 whether the value in RAN4 specification referred by the sample rate X is not changeable by the L1/L2 operation. Question to RAN4: Which parameters influence the value of the sample rate X (i.e. L1 measurement period)? Could RAN4 further indicate if these parameters are changeable by the L1/L2 operation (e.g. BWP switching or SCell activation/deactivation)? 2. Actions: To RAN4: RAN2 respectfully asks RAN4 to answer the above question. 3. Date of Next TSG-RAN WG2 Meetings: TSG-RAN WG2 Meeting #116-bis-e 17 – 25 January 2022 Electronic Meeting TSG-RAN WG2 Meeting #117-e 21 February – 3 March 2022 Electronic Meeting

The following companies provide their observations based on their own simulation results. [DCM] Observation 1: The handover rate of UAV UEs in some cases (e.g., 50m) is higher than that of the terrestrial UEs. Observation 2: The handover failure rate of UAV UEs in some cases (e.g., 50m with 30km/h, 300m with 160km/h) is higher than that of the terrestrial UEs. Observation 3: The ping-pong rate of UAV UEs is lower than that of the terrestrial UEs. Based on our observations, it is proposed that RAN2 should study further the mobility enhancements for UAV UEs to improve the handover performance. [Huawei] Observation 1: The handover rate of the drone UE is nearly 2 times higher than that of the terrestrial UE. Then the trend of simulation results indicated that the UE height has a significant impact on the HO performance, and the drone UE suffers higher HO rate than the terrestrial UE. Observation 2: The HOF rate of the drone UE is at most 17 times higher than that of the terrestrial UE. Then the trend of simulation results indicated that the UE height has a significant impact on the HO performance, and the drone UE suffers much higher HOF rate than the terrestrial UE. Observation 3: The RLF rate of the drone UE is higher than that of the terrestrial UE. Then the trend of simulation results indicated that the UE height has a significant impact on the RLF performance, and the drone UE suffers much higher RLF rate than the terrestrial UE. Observation 4: The time in handoff of the drone UE is higher than that of the terrestrial UE. Then the trend of simulation results indicated that the drone UE experiences much longer time in handoff than the terrestrial UE. Observation 5: The time in Qout of the drone UE is higher than that of the terrestrial UE. Then the trend of simulation results indicated that the drone UE experiences much longer time in Qout than the terrestrial UE. Observation 6: The Ping-Pong rate of the drone UE is slightly higher than that of the terrestrial UE. For RMa scenario only two companies provide simulation results, and the results are gathered and compiled into the same figure for every KPI. {"chunk_id":"R2-2205234-001","collection":"ran2_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["CATT"],"tdocNumber":"R2-2205234","title":"Discussion on the parameters influencing SI modification procedure"},"point_id":"2000309275454209831"}
In this contribution, the parameters in SIB19 that influence SI modification procedure are discussed. Firstly, according to the agreements, the parameters that influence SI modification procedure are analyzed and summarized. Then the corresponding modifications to TS 38.331 are proposed. In past meetings, RAN2 had reached the following agreements: Agreement in RAN2#116bis: Agreement in RAN2#117: “This field is excluded when determining changes in system information, i.e. changes of XXX should neither result in system information change notifications nor in a modification of valueTag in SIB1.”

{"chunk_id":"R2-2306136-001","collection":"ran2_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Xiaomi"],"tdocNumber":"R2-2306136","title":"Discussion on flight path reporting for NR UAV"},"point_id":"1543491594883363060"}
A revised WID on NR support for UAV (Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles) [1] has been approved. In the WID, one objective is to enhance measurement reports, including flight path reporting. In previous meetings [2-6], the following agreements have been reached for flight path reporting for NR UAV: In this contribution, we will provide our understandings on the flight path reporting for NR UAV. The meanings of waypoint and timestamp has reached consensus in previous meetings. However, which waypoints should be included in the flight path information is FFS. Some options have been provided in previous meetings, e.g. the flight path information follows the granularity of the waypoints (i.e. the distance or interval between consecutive waypoints) configured by network and/or provides the information on the destination of the flight. However, it is uncertain whether UE has full flight path information or not e.g. whether the flight path information stored in UE includes the destination of flight and can satisfy the granularity configured by network. And the size and speed of UAV UE may influence over the granularity of waypoint. Hence, whether the requirement of flight path information configured by network can be fulfilled or not depend on the flight path information in UE. It may be difficult to configured appropriate requirements to UE to limit the content of flight path information. And, in LTE UAV, which waypoints are included in flight path information is up to UE implementation. Therefore, no optimization for the content of flight path information is needed for NR UAV. Proposal 1: It is up to UE implementation which waypoints are included in flight path information.

{"chunk_id":"R2-2305948-002","collection":"ran2_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Intel"],"tdocNumber":"R2-2305948","title":"Discussion on NR SL Carrier Aggregation"},"point_id":"6823640801615544949"}
This contribution discusses details on support of SL carrier aggregation and makes the following observations and proposals: Observation 1: After unicast link establishment and L2 ID update, the AS layer can keep track of the changed L2 IDs, either by mapping to PC5 link identifier or by implementation to avoid ambiguity between service and initial vs changed L2 ID. Proposal 1: RAN2 agrees to extend the principle of CBR based TX carrier (re-)selection procedure and LCP restriction based on CBR threshold for unicast. Proposal 2: RAN2 is proposed to discuss how to define criteria for NR SL packet duplication (i.e. to replace PPPR from LTE SL): Based on configured mapping of standardized PQI values, such that only packets belonging to QoS flow with specific PQI value shall be duplicated Based on configured mapping to specific Packet Error Rate (PER) values, such that packets belonging to QoS flow with PER lower than a (pre-)configured threshold shall be duplicated

{"chunk_id":"R2-2502890-001","collection":"ran2_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["MediaTek"],"tdocNumber":"R2-2502890","title":"Discussion on XR rate control"},"point_id":"11506003139951698443"}
This document discusses the objective: uplink congestion control in R19 XR WID [1]. - Specify uplink congestion signalling [RAN2, RAN3]: - Specify in MAC layer XR rate control signalling over downlink per QoS flow/per DRB and the associated F1 signalling, if any, to enable faster source rate adaption to uplink congestion. In RAN plenary #105 meeting [2], companies bring a joint contribution to elaborate that RAN-Aware XR Rate Control is important to XR user experience. Compare to packet drop due to congestion problem which leads to broken image, reducing the data rate (lower resolution but not broken image) has lower negative impact to user experience. Therefore, to know whether there is congestion along the path to destination or not is important for XR services. In RAN2 #128 meeting [3], we already agreed that ”Rate indication from gNB to the UE on a per QoS flow level is supported.” The FFS part is the exact signalling mechanism we adopted, two mechanisms are listed during RAN2 #128 meeting: 1) flows are indicated by MAC CE or 2) by RRC while MAC CE is per DRB. In MAC spec, we already have Recommended bit rate MAC CE to indicate the data rate. However, the granularity of current Recommended bit rate MAC CE is per logical channel (per DRB), which is not finer enough to support XR services, which might have multiple QoS mapped into the same DRB/logical. Another reason is that if we still adopt the second option, there is no difference between legacy Recommended bit rate MAC CE and the new rate indication MAC CE. Therefore, it is better to use QoS flow ID rather than logical channel ID, and according to TS 38.331, the maxQFI is 63, 6 bits is enough to cover all QoS Flow ID. Proposal 1: RAN2 agree to define a new MAC CE, the new MAC CE include 6 bits to indicate QoS Flow ID This document promulgated the following proposals: Proposal 1: RAN2 agree to define a new MAC CE, the new MAC CE include 6 bits to indicate QoS Flow ID [1] RP-250107, Revised WID on XR (eXtended Reality) for NR Phase 3, Nokia (Rapporteur). [2] RP-242224, On RAN Awareness and UL Rate Control for XR, Meta, CATT, CMCC, Google, vivo, ZTE Corporation, Sanechips, Huawei, HiSilicon, Spreadtrum, Samsung, Apple, MediaTek Inc., Futurewei [3] R2-2410915, Report from session on R18 MBS, R18 QoE and R19 XR, Session chair (Huawei).
